Module 1

Introduction to Brain Connectivity : Brain structure vs. function, Types of connectivity: Structural, functional, and effective Relevance in neuropsychiatric disorders (e.g., MDD, ADHD, etc.). Module 2: Neuroimaging Fundamentals : Overview of Neuroimaging modalities such fMRI, EEG, MEG, fNIRS, PET etc. Vascular System of the brain, Coupling of Blood flow and Neuronal activity, BOLD fMRI signal and its correlation with Neuronal signal, Linearity of Hemodynamic response. Module 3: Preprocessing of fMRI: Preprocessing pipeline (motion correction, registration, filtering), Atlases: AAL, Schaefer, Brainnetome, Experimental Design. Module 4: Experimental designs : Block design, Event-related design, Mixed designs (hybrid of block and event-related), Stimulus and Task Design, Experimental Conditions, Data Acquisition Considerations. Module 5: Regression Analysis: Use of general linear model, Modeling of Neuronal activity. Intersubject analyses. Data exploration approaches such as PCA, ICA and Partial least squares. Module 6: Functional connectivity FC matrices: construction and interpretation, Static vs. dynamic connectivity, Time-varying connectivity, Clustering and state-based analysis. Module 7: Network Science for Connectomics: Graph theory fundamentals (nodes, edges, centrality, modularity), Brain network metrics (small-worldness, efficiency, hubs), Community detection (Louvain, Infomap). Module 8: Advanced Topics: Deep learning for FC, Individual fingerprinting & functional gradients, Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD), Brain Stimulation and neurofeedback and its effect in Brain Functional Connectivity.

Review of digital signal processing

Discrete-time signals and systems, transform representation of signals and systems, auditory models, lossless tube models fundamentals of digital filters, sampling. Fundamentals of human hearing and speech perception, Speech production, short-time Fourier transform, acoustic phonetics, Anatomy and functions of the ear, the perception of sound, auditory models, lossless tube models. Time-domain and Frequency-domain methods for speech processing Short-time analysis (energy, magnitude, zero-crossing rate, autocorrelation), Discrete-time Fourier analysis, short-time Fourier analysis, spectrograms, Overlap-add method of synthesis, filter-bank summation method of synthesis. Cepstrum and homomorphic speech processing Homomorphic analysis, computing the short time cepstrum and the complex cepstrum, cepstrum analysis of all-pole models, cepstrum distance measures. Linear predictive analysis of speech Basic ideas, gain computation, frequency-domain interpretation, solving LPC equations, the prediction error signal. representations of LP. Algorithms for estimating speech parameters Median smoothing, speech-background discrimination, pitch period estimation, formant estimation. Applications: speech recognition, speech enhancement, speaker recognition, Hidden Markov models for speech recognition, statistical methods for speech enhancement, factor analysis for speaker recognition.

Module 1 RL Foundations & Dynamic Programming - Theory

Agent-environment-reward framework, Markov Decision Processes: returns, value functions and Bellman equations: policy evaluation, policy improvement, policy iteration and value iteration. Lab: Build a GridWorld/FrozenLake MDP
implement policy iteration and value iteration
visualise value functions and optimal policy. Module 2 Monte Carlo & Temporal Difference Methods - Theory

Monte Carlo prediction and control- on-policy vs off-policy learning (brief importance sampling): TD(O), SARSA, Q-learning. Lab: Tabular MC control, SARSA and Q-learning on FrozenLake/Taxi/CliffWalking
compare on-policy vs off-policy behaviour. Module 3 DeepRL

Value-Based & Policy-Gradient Foundations - Theory: Function approximation, neural-network value functions: Deep Q-Networks: experience replay and target networks, policy- gradient theorem - REINFORCE. Lab: DQN on CartPole to LunarLander (replay buffer + target net)
REINFORCE on CartPole. Module 4 Actor-Critic & Advanced Deep RL - Theory

Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C): deterministic policy gradients and DDPG - TD3 - Soft Actor-Critic and entropy regularization, exploration strategies (ε- greedy, entropy-based). Lah: A2C on a discrete task
SAC or TD3 on Pendulum I continuous control (Stable-Baselines3). Module 5 Model-Based, Multi-Agent, Exploration & Safe RL - Theory

Environment-dynamics modeling and planning (Dyna-Q) - cooperative vs competitive MARL: MADDPG and QMIX (overview) - curiosity- driven exploration - meta-RL and transfer (brief) - safe/constrained RL. Lab: Dyna-Q planning
one multi-agent or curiosity-driven task (PettingZoo or exploration-bonus agent). Module 6 Advanced RL

PPO, DPO & RLHF - Theory: Trust regions and Proximal Policy Optimization - preference-based RL-Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: reward modeling and the RLHF pipeline- Direct Preference Optimization - alignment of large models. Lab: PPO (from scratch or SB3) on LunarLander/custom env
mini RLHF/DPO pipeline on a small language model using HuggingFace TRL with a tiny preference dataset. Courses offered in the Discipline of Electric Vehicle Technology
